node.title: Re: Referencing the locals
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
${a} is just another way to write $a ([doc://perldata]). ${'a'} is a [doc://perlref#Symbolic-references|symbolic reference]. The latter is forbidden under [doc://strict], and that's a good thing, as it can easily cause all kinds of hard-to-debug chaos (Update: [id://1213425|one example]). See also [id://111088].

The typical case where I want to use it is when I have a handful of arrays and want to do stuff with each of them ... How can I reference the local ones?

No, you don't want to ;-) You likely want a hash of arrays instead ([doc://perldsc]).

my %animals = ( cat => [1,2,3], dog => [5,6], pig => [4,3,2,1], );

See also [https://perl.plover.com/varvarname.html|Why it's stupid to `use a variable as a variable name'].
